findings.severityBasis: Trivy selected HIGH; its retained vendor severities record Red Hat and Photon as HIGH and Ubuntu as MEDIUM, while the OpenSSL advisory rates the issue Low.
findings.reachability: The advisory requires an application-created OpenSSL QUIC server. The assessed weed mini topology is TCP-only, publishes no UDP listener, and does not use OpenSSL as a QUIC server.
findings.disposition: Policy failure: an exception may be technically eligible, but no explicit reviewed exception was requested or accepted for this candidate.
requiredMitigationsIfReassessed: Do not run an application-created OpenSSL QUIC listener and assert that no UDP listener or UDP port exposure exists.
Expire the exception on any digest or topology change or when a rebuilt stable image is available.

blockingFindings.requirement: Opaque exact S3 keys and complete ordinal listing
blockingFindings.description: Release 4.44 cannot reliably preserve an object whose key is also a prefix of another key. Depending on write order it rejects the prefix object or loses or hides it during exact reads and listing.
blockingFindings.mitigation: None without restricting the unrestricted key accepted by the provider-neutral interface, weakening exact-key integrity and listing, or rebuilding the provider.

blockingFindings.requirement: Partial-request isolation and W4 concurrent upload behavior
blockingFindings.description: An abandoned request can close the shared filer connection and cancel unrelated concurrent multipart uploads.
blockingFindings.mitigation: None at the deployment boundary without weakening the required concurrency and fault gates.

blockingFindings.description: Release 4.44 returns PreconditionFailed for a conditional GET or HEAD of a missing object instead of preserving missing-object semantics.
blockingFindings.mitigation: A second HEAD would be racy and would weaken the merged provider-neutral failure contract.

blockingFindings.requirement: Conditional streamed get, normalized failures, integrity, and accurate runtime signals
blockingFindings.description: Release 4.44 commits HTTP 200 or 206 and records time-to-first-byte before the first volume read succeeds. A missing or corrupt first needle therefore surfaces as a broken success body instead of a clean provider failure.
blockingFindings.mitigation: None at the deployment boundary; the application cannot replace an already committed provider success response with the required normalized failure.

blockingFindings.requirement: Pinned durability behavior and process-kill/restart recovery
blockingFindings.description: Release 4.44 computes a storage rule's fsync setting in the filer but does not propagate it to S3 PUT, multipart, or copy uploads. S3 writes configured for fsync are acknowledged to the client without requesting fsync from the volume server.
blockingFindings.mitigation: None without rebuilding the provider or weakening the required acknowledged-write durability and recovery gate.

boundedFindings.description: A named static identity file that parses to zero identities leaves release 4.44 open to anonymous S3 operations.
boundedFindings.requiredMitigationIfReassessed: Semantically validate an exact non-empty bucket-scoped identity document before startup, mount it read-only, reject environment-admin credentials, keep S3 private, and require anonymous-denial plus signed-access readiness probes.

boundedFindings.description: Release 4.44 can surface a filer transport failure after a delete was committed instead of replaying it internally.
boundedFindings.disposition: Not independently blocking because the merged application boundary classifies ambiguous mutations and requires caller convergence, but a later candidate must still pass the fault gate.
